title: Proxy-Validated Importance-Aware Federated Sample Selection with Meta Learning

problem.claim: Federated data selection aims to choose high-quality samples to improve federated learning convergence and reduce resource overhead.

gap.claim: Existing studies do not account for dynamically changing sample importance or depend on external unbiased validation datasets, which may hinder real-world application.

contributions.claim: FedSelect is a proxy-validated, importance-aware federated sample selection framework.
FedSelect uses meta learning with a proxy validation dataset to select important clients and samples.
The framework includes a momentum-based meta-margin function for discovering influential proxy samples and an online meta-model update strategy.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe FedSelect, its meta learning approach, and its momentum-based meta-margin function as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four benchmark datasets reportedly show that FedSelect is superior in effectiveness and efficiency.
The authors report strong scalability across diverse scenarios.
Source code is reported to be available in a public repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated sample selection is positioned as a way to improve convergence and reduce resource overhead.
Prior approaches overlook dynamic sample importance or require external unbiased validation data, creating potential performance and deployment concerns.
FedSelect applies proxy-validated importance-aware selection through meta learning over clients and samples.
A momentum-based meta-margin function supplies proxy validation samples and adaptive rewards, while online meta-model updates support efficiency.
Benchmark experiments reportedly indicate effectiveness, efficiency, and scalability advantages.

source_observation.claim: The framework replaces external unbiased validation data with influential samples discovered through a momentum-based meta-margin function.

interpretation.claim: A system may reduce deployment dependencies by constructing an adaptive proxy signal from the data-selection process itself.

application.claim: For decentralized or data-constrained optimization, investigate adaptive internal validation signals before requiring globally available validation data.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when internally generated proxy validation is reliable across domains or data distributions.

source_observation.claim: FedSelect combines importance-aware selection with online meta-model updates.

interpretation.claim: Selection quality and operational efficiency are treated as coupled design objectives.

application.claim: When optimizing iterative distributed systems, pair decision-quality mechanisms with update strategies that control their runtime cost.

exception.claim: The abstract does not quantify the tradeoff between selection quality, update overhead, and scalability.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four benchmark datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the federated data-partition assumptions or client-selection protocol.
The abstract does not provide details about the meta-learning objective, convergence behavior, or computational overhead.
